answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require a proof-of-worked identity: before an agent joins, it must solve a public computational puzzle — e.g., plotting a comet trajectory against a shared orbital atlas — and publish the result for stake-weighted peers to verify. Like a market that only opens at dawn, entry is open to everyone, but the cost is paid in compute. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities pays that cost thousands of times over, so a sybil flood becomes linearly expensive, while a single honest agent pays it once.
